titulo: Strategies: paraphrasing, asking for help and buying time: Asking for help, repetition and clarification

aula.titulo: Strategies: paraphrasing, asking for help and buying time
aula.objetivo: Keep the conversation going when a word is missing: explain it in other words (paraphrase), ask politely for repetition and clarification, check what you've understood and buy time to think without going silent.

sessao.titulo: Asking for help, repetition and clarification

blocos.titulo: Asking for repetition, asking for help and checking
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: to ask someone to repeat, use «¿Puedes repetirlo?» (tú) or «¿Puede repetirlo, por favor?» (usted). People also say «¿Cómo dices?» and «¿Cómo dice?»; in speech «¿Perdón?» or «¿Cómo?» is enough (like English "Sorry?" or "Pardon?"). In some countries, such as Mexico, you hear «¿Mande?» instead of «¿Cómo?». STEP 2: to ask someone to speak slowly, use «más despacio»: «¿Podría hablar más despacio?». Also: «más alto» (louder, "speak up") and «más claro». STEP 3: to say you haven't understood, use «No lo he entendido» or «No he entendido la última parte». To say you didn't hear properly, say «No te he oído bien»: «oír» is to hear the sound; «escuchar» is to listen; «entender» is to understand. STEP 4: to ask about a meaning or a form, use «¿Qué significa «cronograma»?», «¿Cómo se escribe?» (How do you spell it?), «¿Cómo se pronuncia?» and «¿Cómo se dice «schedule» en español?». There's no «de» after «significa». STEP 5: to check what you've understood, use «¿Quiere decir que…?» (Do you mean that…?), «Entonces, ¿…?», «A ver si lo he entendido: …» (Let me see if I've got this right) and «Si no me equivoco, …». After «a ver si», use the indicative. STEP 6: to ask for help, use «¿Me podría ayudar con…?», «Necesito ayuda con…» and «¿Le importa repetirlo?» (Would you mind repeating it?). STEP 7: pronouns: «¿Puede explicármelo?» and «¿Me lo puede explicar?» mean the same (lesson 60 gives the full rule). STEP 8: finish with «Gracias, ahora lo entiendo» or «Perfecto, ya lo tengo» (Great, got it). That signals the conversation can move on.
blocos.comparacao: English "What do you mean?" is «¿Qué quieres decir?», literally "what do you want to say?"; «¿Qué significa?» is for a word. "How do you spell it?" is «¿Cómo se escribe?». And English "I don't understand anything" is «No entiendo nada» — Spanish needs the «no» before the verb even with «nada».

erros.motivo: «Lentamente» is correct but sounds stiff in conversation; people say «despacio».
The pronoun goes before the conjugated verb or is attached to the infinitive, not in between.
With «nada» after the verb, you need «no» before it.

blocos.enunciado: Make up a short dialogue: someone speaks fast and you (1) ask them to repeat, (2) ask them to speak more slowly, (3) ask what a word means and (4) check what you've understood with «Entonces, ¿quiere decir que…?». Play both parts out loud.
Describe out loud a word you've forgotten, using «sirve para», «es lo contrario de» and «se parece a».
